title: Your Card Says 24.99% APR. That's Not What It Actually Costs You
description:
Your credit card statement quotes a yearly rate called APR. But issuers compound interest daily, not once a year - so the rate that actually hits your balance is higher. We run the real math on a $5,000 balance carried for one year and show the exact dollar gap.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#Shorts #creditcards #APR #personalfinance

segments.text: Your credit card statement says twenty four point nine nine percent APR. That's not actually what carrying a balance costs you.
APR is the stated yearly rate. But card issuers compound interest daily, not once a year. That gap has its own name: APY.
Twenty four point nine nine percent APR actually compounds out to twenty eight point three eight percent APY.
Put that in dollars. Carry a five thousand dollar balance, untouched, for exactly one year.
At the simple APR rate, that's twelve hundred forty nine dollars. What daily compounding actually charges: fourteen hundred nineteen dollars.

slide.headline: Cost of carrying $5,000 for one year

segments.text: That's an extra hundred sixty nine dollars you didn't see coming, purely from how often the interest compounds.
The label and the bill are not the same number.
